reforms.description: Japan introduced a tax credit for incremental R&D expenditures by corporations, providing indirect support for private-sector research and development activities.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Tax credits for incremental R&D reduce the cost of innovation for firms, incentivising additional research investment and productivity improvements.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'introduced', indicating the tax credit was in force by 1999.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant policy instrument targeting private R&D, but narrower in scope than system-wide reforms.
reforms.source_quote: Tax credit for incremental R&D 29 [billion yen]

reforms.description: Japan legislated the Industrial Revitalisation Law (1999), which grants researchers intellectual property rights on government-sponsored research and hands back IP rights to private-sector researchers conducting work on behalf of the government. The law also reduced patent fees for Technology Licensing Organisations and included measures to assist business start-ups through credit insurance without collateral and zero-interest loans.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Clarifying and returning IP rights to researchers and private firms reduces barriers to commercialisation and spinoff creation, incentivising innovation and technology transfer. Reduced patent fees lower transaction costs for TLOs.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'legislated' and 'decided', indicating passage into law but implementation timing not explicitly confirmed.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant legislative reform addressing multiple aspects of knowledge transfer and commercialisation, but not a system-wide structural change.
reforms.source_quote: The government has decided to begin to hand back to private-sector researchers the intellectual property rights on research they have conducted on its behalf in order to encourage them to exploit its potential and thereby strengthen industrial competitiveness. The bill also reduced patent fees for Technology Licensing Organisations.

reforms.description: Japan implemented tax and lending programmes to encourage startup formation and venture business development, including loans and credit insurance programmes for start-ups and venture firms to support private-sector business venture risks and the growth of dynamic small businesses, following the November 1998 Emergency Economic Measures.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Loans and credit insurance reduce financing barriers for startups and venture firms, enabling business formation and growth in the private sector.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'implemented' for both entries, confirming programmes were in force by 1998–1999.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant policy package supporting startup ecosystem, but narrower than system-wide structural reforms.
reforms.source_quote: the government has just made a number of changes that will ease corporate restructuring, promote technological innovation and encourage the private sector to take more business venture risks by, for example, facilitating mergers and acquisitions and employee buyouts, handing back intellectual property rights to private researchers sponsored by the government, and providing loans and credit insurance to start-ups and venture firms

reforms.description: The government established a venture-capital fund programme in partnership with the private sector, with the Small and Medium Enterprise Agency providing 10 billion yen in capital (limited to no more than half of each fund and 1 billion yen per fund) to support promising start-up companies, with private venture-capital companies providing matching funding and management.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Public-private venture capital funds mobilise capital for innovative startups, reducing financing constraints and supporting the commercialisation of new technologies.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'established', indicating the programme was legislated/decided but implementation timing not explicitly confirmed.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant new instrument for startup financing with substantial capital commitment, but narrower than system-wide reforms.
reforms.source_quote: The government is also planning to join with the private sector to set up a series of venture-capital funds to provide cash to promising start-up companies, while private venture-capital companies are to put up half of the 20 billion yen in funding. The funds are to be set up by the Small and Medium Enterprise Agency by the end of March 2000.

reforms.description: The government plans to grant corporate status to 89 state-run research institutions and transform them into semi-autonomous agencies as part of central administrative reorganisation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Corporatisation of research institutions can improve operational efficiency and responsiveness to market needs, but may also reduce long-term basic research investment if autonomy is coupled with performance pressure. The net effect is ambiguous without implementation details.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'plans to grant', indicating the reform was legislated/decided but implementation was planned for 2001 or later.
reforms.importance_rationale: Structural, system-wide reform affecting 89 state-run research institutions and the governance of public research infrastructure.
reforms.source_quote: As part of the reorganisation of the central administrative system, the government plans to grant corporate status to 89 state-run institutions (mostly research institutions) already earmarked for change and intends to transform these institutions into semi-autonomous agencies.
